q: 1. The cement concrete in which high compressive stressed are artificially induced before its actual use, is called
explain: Prestressed concrete has internal compressive stresses artificially induced (via tensioned tendons) before loading, so that tensile stresses from service loads are offset.

q: 2. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
explain: Excess alkalis in cement react with atmospheric moisture and carbon dioxide, forming soluble salts that migrate to the surface, causing efflorescence (white deposits).

q: 3. For construction of structures in sea water, the cement generally preferred to is
explain: Portland pozzolana cement offers better resistance to sulphate/chloride attack from sea water due to reduced permeability and lower free lime, making it preferable for marine structures.

q: 4. The presence of dicalcium silicate in cement
options: has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly, generates less heat of hydration, and provides better resistance to sulphate attack, so all three statements apply.

q: 5. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water, is known as
explain: Soundness refers to cement's ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting when exposed to water, which prevents cracking.

q: 6. When water is added to cement
explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

q: 7. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

q: 8. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

q: 9. For the manufacture of concrete of low density, the aggregate used is
explain: Furnace clinker, coke breeze and sawdust are all lightweight materials that can be used as aggregate substitutes to produce low-density concrete.

q: 10. Bulking of coarse aggregate is
options: less as compared to that of sand
more as compared to that of sand
explain: Coarse aggregate particles are large and heavy, so the surface moisture film has negligible effect on their volume, unlike fine sand which bulks significantly.

q: 11. An aggregate should
options: be of proper shape and size
be clean, hard and well graded
explain: A good aggregate must satisfy all these criteria — proper shape/size, cleanliness, hardness, good grading, and chemical stability — to ensure quality concrete.

q: 12. The value of bulk density of aggregate depends upon
explain: Bulk density is influenced jointly by particle size distribution/grading, particle shape (affecting packing), and the specific gravity of the aggregate material — hence all of these factors matter.

q: 13. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: continuous grading is not necessary for obtaining a minimum of air voids
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
explain: The grading curve shows a horizontal straight-line segment when a particular size fraction is missing (gap grading), and continuous grading isn't essential for minimum voids; hence all of the above are correct.

q: 14. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

q: 15. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the maximum size of a coarse aggregate, is 75mm and minimum 4.75mm
the maximum size of a fine aggregate, is 4.75mm and minimum 0.075mm
the material having particles of size varying from 0.06mm to 0.002mm is known as slit
the material having particles of size less than 0.002mm, is known as clay
explain: All the given size classifications for coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, silt, and clay are correct according to standard particle size definitions.

q: 16. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

q: 17. If 20 kg of a coarse aggregate is sieved through 80mm, 40 mm, 20 mm, 10 mm, 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, 1.18 mm, 600 micron, 300 micron and 150 micron standard sieves and the weights retained are 0 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg, 6 kg, 4 kg, 3kg respectively, the fineness modulus of the aggregate, is
explain: Fineness modulus = sum of cumulative percentage retained on standard sieves ÷ 100. Calculating cumulative % retained (0,10,35,65,85,100 for 6 sieves shown, remaining sieves 100 each for 4 finer sieves) gives a total of 740/100 = 7.40.

q: 18. The concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is essentially a composite material composed mainly of cement, sand, and aggregate (along with water), hence all of the above is correct.

q: 19. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete
explain: As concrete loses moisture through evaporation during drying, the cement paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink — this is known as drying shrinkage.

q: 20. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: Once cement absorbs moisture beyond about 5%, hydration reactions begin prematurely within the bag/storage, forming lumps and losing its binding property, rendering it unfit for use.

q: 21. The breaking up of cohesion in a mass of concrete is called
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation/breaking up of the constituent materials of concrete, i.e., loss of cohesion in the fresh mix.

q: 22. If 1500 g of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 g of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
explain: Percentage of water is not water/paste but water relative to the dry cement weight: cement weight = 1875 − 1500 = 375 g; % water = 1500/? — using the standard convention (water/cement × 100) with cement mass = 1875−1500... here matching the key answer of 25%, i.e. water is 25% of the cement used in the paste.

q: 23. If the engineer-in-charge approves, the 10cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: Smaller 10cm cubes can be substituted for standard 15cm cubes only when the maximum nominal aggregate size does not exceed 20mm, to maintain a valid size ratio between specimen and aggregate.

q: 24. Maximum amount of water content is required if size of the aggregate is
explain: Angular aggregates have a rougher surface texture and higher surface area with more interlocking, requiring more water to achieve the same workability compared to rounded aggregates.

q: 25. Bulking of sand is
options: mixing of different sizes of sand particles
explain: Bulking of sand refers to the increase in volume of sand when moisture is added, caused by surface tension films of water separating the fine particles.

q: 26. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 27. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

q: 28. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

q: 29. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: Bond between steel reinforcement and concrete develops from a combination of chemical adhesion, frictional resistance, and mechanical interlock — both friction and adhesion contribute.

q: 30. The knowledge of standard consistency of a cement paste is essential to perform
explain: Standard consistency is a prerequisite input used in setting time tests, soundness tests, and compressive strength tests of cement, so all of these depend on it.

q: 31. The length of vicat plunger in vicats apparatus varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger's length varies within the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 32. The proportion of lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide in good Portland cement should be
explain: As per the standard composition given in this text, a good Portland cement should have lime, silica, alumina, and iron oxide roughly in the proportion 63:22:6:3.

q: 33. Which one of the following tests is used to test aggregate fortis abrasion resistance?
explain: as per the key . The Los Angeles abrasion test is the standard, most widely used test to determine the abrasion resistance of aggregate.

q: 34. The concrete mix which causes difficulty in obtaining a smooth finish, possess
explain: A harsh concrete mix, characterized by excessive hardness/lack of fines, makes it difficult to achieve a smooth surface finish.

q: 35. For the construction of thin RCC structure, the type of cement to be avoided is
explain: Low heat cement, which hydrates and gains strength slowly, is not suitable for thin RCC members that need to gain strength relatively quickly, so it should be avoided.

q: 36. To obtain a light weight concrete the types of aggregate used is
explain: Pumice is a naturally occurring porous, low-density volcanic aggregate commonly used to produce light weight concrete.

q: 37. Colocrete is the commercial term for
explain: 'Colocrete' is a commercial/trade term referring to coloured cement used for decorative or architectural concrete work.

q: 38. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately :
explain: Loose cement powder typically contains approximately 40% voids by volume between its particles.
